messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: 🚨 High GPU queue growth detected for pool `us-west-2/gpu-pool-a` — autoscaler failing to add capacity (SLO breach risk). Alert: https://redwood/alerts/6215554321
Devon H: saw this — getting paged. I'm checking autoscaler and allocator logs now.
Devon H: quick snapshot: queue length up to 18k reqs, median latency 2.3s -> 8.7s over last 6m, error spike retries 5xx.
Sara K: assigning to oncall (cheng) and ops (marcus). @Cheng L can you take primary?
Cheng L: on it. looking at autoscaler: `scale_request: 0 -> 0` repeatedly, reason: "scale capped by max_nodes for pool". config shows max_nodes=120, current=120.
Marcus P: confirmed — pool at max_nodes. But we've got ~25% of GPUs unusable due to MIG fragmentation; allocator logs show many small free slices but not matching requested slice sizes.
Devon H: logs: `allocator: no compatible slot found for request model=llama-13b mig_profile=7g.40gb` repeated. Many requests are medium-slice; we've got many 1g/2g fragments.
Elaine R: customer impact: several high-traffic customers (org-42 and realtime-chat) showing degraded response times, SLAs at risk. Support alerted.
support-bot: Notified org-42 and org-99 support pages, sent initial message template. Ticket created: TCK-8732.
Cheng L: quick mitigation plan — try two-pronged: 1) emergency scale override to bump max_nodes by +20 (if cloud quota allows). 2) reduce requested MIG profile for lower-priority workloads and force-evict/relocate them to burst pool.
Devon H: cloud quotas: we only have +8 GPUs available in region. Request to cloud infra for extra quota in flight (support case #CLOUD-1123).
Marcus P: while waiting on quota, we can repack MIG sizes on a subset of nodes to reduce fragmentation. Risk: node-level evictions will cause transient failures for some jobs.
Elaine R: prioritize routing/latency SLA customers to Dedicated pool fallback? We have capacity in dedicated-reserve in us-west but needs manual routing switch.
Cheng L: I'm going to start a targeted repack on low-priority pools and flip eviction threshold to 0.6 to allow more aggressive binpacking. Command:

```
# run repack for pool-a nodes subset
./infractl repack --pool us-west-2/gpu-pool-a --selector 'tag=batch' --dry-run=false
kubectl annotate nodes <node-list> repack=force
```

Cheng L: starting now. I'll stream logs here.
Devon H: I'm also pushing a temporary autoscaler override: `max_nodes=140` for pool-a; will monitor. If cloud quota blocks, I'll revert.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: autoscaler override requested by Devon H; status: pending quota check. See https://redwood/actions/6215554321
Marcus P: repack job started, first node set finishing drain: eviction events kicking off. Expect 2-3 minute pod restarts for batch jobs.
Cheng L: allocator logs during repack: `repack: moved 6 slices, freed 2 full 40GB MIGs` — that's promising.
Elaine R: report from support: org-42 latency improved from 8.7s -> 4.1s after initial repack + routing changes. Still above baseline.
Devon H: cloud quota update — support confirmed +12 GPUs available, so override to 132 applied. Autoscaler now scaling up, new nodes provisioning.
Marcus P: new nodes have mixed MIG configs; need to ensure scheduler can place medium-slice requests. Observed some placement failures still: `no bin for request size 2g on node X`.
Cheng L: I temporarily enabled fallback to allow model-policy to accept 1g slices for non-latency-critical requests. Adjusted policy with:

```
model-routing:set --model llama-13b --allow-fallback-sizes=1g,2g
```

Cheng L: doing this only for batch and background traffic.
Devon H: queue length started to decrease — 18k -> 6.5k over 12m. Latency trending down.
incident-bot: PAGE NOTE: On-call handoff scheduled — Cheng L -> Marcus P at 6215554500 (next rotation).
Marcus P: taking secondary. keeping watch on packing metrics and autoscaler events.
Elaine R: customer comms: Sent follow-up to org-42 noting degraded performance and mitigation steps. Support ticket updated with ETA for full recovery ~45m.
support-bot: org-99 replied: they saw transient errors earlier but are stable now. Marked as monitoring.
Cheng L: post-repack allocator state: freed capacity: 14 x 40GB-equivalent slices. Effective usable GPUs back to ~96%.
Devon H: final autoscaler state: pool nodes 132 (target), serving capacity increased. Monitoring for churn.
Marcus P: scheduling still shows a slow trickle of placement failures for a handful of medium-slice requests — opening follow-up task to align MIG profiles and improve binpacking heuristics: INFRA-1629.
Elaine R: summary for ops: root cause = combination of pool at configured max_nodes + MIG fragmentation (many small leftover slices) -> autoscaler couldn't add nodes and scheduler couldn't place medium-slice workloads leading to queue growth and throttling.
Elaine R: mitigation list: 1) increased max_nodes (temporary), 2) targeted repack to consolidate slices, 3) enabled fallback sizing for non-critical traffic, 4) cloud quota request fulfilled, 5) manual routing of high-SLA customers to dedicated pool.
Devon H: immediate incident state: mitigated, not yet resolved. Will keep thread open until metrics stable for 1h past last spike.
Cheng L: creating postmortem checklist and linking playbook items to INFRA-1629. I'll take primary for the postmortem write-up.
Marcus P: adding action item to review default MIG profiles and autoscaler max_nodes policies — probably relax hard caps or add auto-raise path when fragmentation > 15%.
Elaine R: support follow-ups: update customers in TCK-8732 with root cause and ETA. I'll draft the message.
incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: Severity lowered to P2 at 6215554580. Continue monitoring.
Devon H: thanks all. Kudos to the repack + autoscaler team. I'll update the incident channel once we hit stable.
